A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same visual-thought study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, human ratings of visual-thought quality, attention analyses, and information-flow interventions in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds prompting controls, noise-sensitivity experiments, additional model analyses, and ensemble evaluations.

M1.justification: The four visual-thought procedures and their prompts remain unchanged. Appendix E adds an implemented Diverse-VT strategy that ensembles diverse visual-thought reasoning paths on GPT-4o, a limited procedural extension despite its placement under Future Work.

E1.justification: The represented datasets and task families remain MMVP, V*Bench, M3CoT-Commonsense, CoMT, IsoBench, and ScienceQA. Added experiments vary prompting, tool parameters, model configurations, and inference aggregation within this coverage; no additional dataset or distinct task population is established.

E2.justification: v2 adds a GPT-4o w/o CoT comparator in Table 3 and single-form Maj@4 comparators for Diverse-VT in Table 4. Figure 11 also adds a Direct-versus-w/o-VT prompting comparison. The comparator membership in the original main table remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include tool-parameter sweeps assessed using MLLM evaluation and CLIPScore, an intact-context prompting control, and Maj@4 comparisons. Attention analysis expands to LLaVA-1.5 7B/13B and Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B with layer-percentage and attention-difference summaries; saliency analysis adds Qwen2-VL-2B. These substantially extend the protocols while retaining the original main evaluations.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of external-tool noise, contextual-perturbation confounding, CoT removal, model architecture/size, and visual-thought ensembling. It also replaces v1's two-example saliency analysis with a cross-model comparison on one example, removing the ocean case and the image-to-query and image-to-visual-thought pathways.

E5.justification: Figure 6 retains the same correlations, p-values, and shaded regression bands. The new checklist discusses existing uncertainty coverage, but no new seeds, repeated-experiment counts, or uncertainty estimators are reported. Maj@4 specifies inference aggregation rather than statistical replication.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 are numerically unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results under new conditions, including GPT-4o w/o CoT averaging 57.43 in Table 3 and Diverse-VT averaging 64.80 in Table 4. New figures report noise, prompting-control, and cross-model findings. The retained pure-text plot also reverses image-form/text-form rankings, including MATH-Convexity, between v1 Figure 10 and v2 Figure 12 without explanation.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(9), including the visual-thought formulation, attention averaging, and saliency calculation, retain their mathematical substance. v2 clarifies the interpretation of saliency-matrix entries but introduces no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: visual thoughts unify explanations of MCoT, their four expressions differ in effectiveness, and they mediate visual information into deeper layers. Additional experiments and the appendix ensemble do not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning failure under excessive tool noise, architecture/depth having greater influence than parameter count, and weak textual visual thoughts arising from LLaVA's language limitations. It also distinguishes the effects of removing CoT and removing visual thoughts. These expand the mechanism explanations and applicability qualifications beyond v1's retained cache account.

D1.justification: v2 documents Stable Diffusion v1.5, threshold/guidance settings, and model configurations for added analyses. Its checklist newly states that code is unavailable and planned for later release. Original prompts and hardware disclosures remain, while the explicit caption-construction detail for pure-text problems is removed; the new ensemble remains sparsely specified.

R1.justification: v2 adds the ViTCoT video-text interleaved chain-of-thought reference to the related-work discussion. The existing literature coverage and positioning around a unified explanation of textual and interleaved MCoT otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes comprise localized wording edits, updated affiliations and publication information, acknowledgements, a NeurIPS checklist, and additional appendix subsections, including Future Work.

P2.justification: v2 adds noise and prompting-control figures and two tables, substantially expands the attention figure, and redesigns the saliency figure around a cross-model comparison. It also revises diagram typography and Figure 4's axis presentation. These display changes go beyond renumbering and numerical updates.

improvement.justification: The intact-context control, no-CoT baseline, noise tests, and broader model analyses strengthen evidence concerning confounding, failure conditions, and generality. The net improvement is limited by incomplete specifications of added experiments, removal of two information-flow pathways and one case, and the unexplained image/text-form ranking reversal in the retained pure-text figure. These tradeoffs prevent a substantial overall quality gain.
